nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (Weekly)
nodes.notes: Fires weekly, Monday 6am. Adjust cadence in the interval field to match how often the client actually receives new data.

nodes.name: Call /api/refresh
nodes.notes: Replace YOUR-RENDER-APP with the actual deployed Render URL once live. Timeout set to 120s since Render's free tier can cold-start (30-60s) before the pipeline itself even runs.

nodes.name: Alert recommended?
nodes.notes: True branch fires when EITHER change_detection.material_change OR drift_check.drift_detected is true — same compound-condition pattern as the sentiment pipeline's IF node.

nodes.name: Send Alert

parameters.subject: Ops Analytics: refresh flagged for review

nodes.notes: Swap for a Slack node if preferred — same pattern as the sentiment pipeline's Gmail alert node. Configure sender/recipient credentials before running.

nodes.name: No Action Needed
nodes.notes: Refresh completed silently — no material change and no model drift. This is the expected outcome on most runs.

meta.description: Dual-trigger refresh workflow: Manual Trigger for on-demand runs, Schedule Trigger for automatic weekly refreshes. Both feed the same downstream chain, so there is exactly one refresh logic path to maintain, not two. The Flask API's /api/refresh endpoint does the actual work (feature engineering, drift check, insight ranking, conditional LLM write-up); this workflow's only job is triggering it and routing the result to an alert or not.
